Will AI take my job is the same question as "will computers take my job" when the UNIVAC came on the scene. We were just at the beginning of the computer era and didn't know what computers would be able to do or how people's jobs would eventually integrate them. Same with AI today. We're just scratching the surface. When the UNIVAC hit the scene, who knew "computers" would eventually bring about word processors replacing typewriters and spreadsheets replacing written ledgers? It's the different use cases of AI that we haven't even discovered yet that will be the most revolutionary in the next 10-20 years. AI will do what most every other improvement to productivity and efficiency has done - it won't mean fewer people making the same output, it will mean the same or more people creating more output.
